subject: Follow-up: Discovery recap and a couple quick integration questions
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@lumenhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + one small ask on integration

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the candidness about your priorities for patient-facing summarization and the constraints around PHI retention. Quick recap on what we discussed and two small questions that would help us scope a pilot properly: 

Recap (high level)
- Goal: Improve patient message clarity and triage at intake; reduce average response time for basic questions.
- Primary constraints: On-prem data access for PHI, per-request latency SLO ~500ms, budget guidance ~medium (pilot).
- Potential nodes: Inference in VPC with optional private deployment later.

Two quick questions for scope (would love a 1–2 line answer):
1) Integration surface: do you expect the inference to sit behind your API gateway (existing microservice) or as a sidecar in the intake service?
2) Data samples: can you share a redacted snippet of the intake messages format (or confirm CSV/JSON schema)? that will help us recommend batch sizes and tokenization strategy.

Next step proposal: 15-min technical sync with your engineering lead + our platform engineer to validate the integration approach. I’m available Mon/Tue afternoon PT — if that works, I can send a calendar invite.

I attached a one-pager and a short integration matrix that maps common integration patterns to our recommendations.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

[Attachment: Redwood-one-pager.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: integration-matrix.xlsx (Excel)]

Hi Alex —

Thanks — apologies for the delay. We’re still lining up internal priorities for Q1; the short answers below to help you: 

1) Integration surface: likely behind our API gateway initially. Our intake service team prefers not to add sidecars for the pilot.
2) Data samples: I can share a redacted JSON schema (no PHI) — attaching the schema we use for intake records.

We’re still evaluating whether the pilot will be on-prem or in our VPC; procurement will need the SOW and an outline of the retention model. If you can send a short SOW + sample S3 retention policy, I’ll route to procurement.

Samira
Samira Khan

samira@lumenhealth.ai

Hi Samira —

Perfect — thank you for the quick answers and for the schema. That clarifies the integration approach. Next actions from our side: 

- I’ll share a short SOW draft (1 page) with the pilot scope and retention language by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa (cc’d) will propose two calendar windows for a 15-min technical sync with your intake lead and our platform engineer.
- Grace will include a redwood-hosted sample retention policy and an example DocuSign link we use for pilot contracts.

If it helps procurement, here are bullet points they usually ask for:
- Pilot duration: 6 weeks
- Data flow: redwood Dedicated in VPC with optional on-prem connector for PHI (per sample SOW)
- SLAs: 99.5% uptime for inference endpoints during pilot, 95th percentile p95 latency target 500ms (per request)
- Billing: monthly invoices for reserved pilot capacity + usage overage

I’ll attach the SOW + retention example to the HubSpot record and send the DocuSign link when it’s ready.

Would you prefer a Tuesday 11/09 2:30pm PT or Wednesday 11/10 11:00am PT slot? If neither works, share a couple windows and we’ll flex.

Best —
Alex
